definition: InhabitedConcreteAt m concrete w is ∃ b, concrete b ∧ m.ExistsAt w b over the Kant/#487 Ontic signature: some member of the constant candidate domain satisfies the supplied concreteness predicate and exists at w. concrete : E → Prop is unconstrained and not world-indexed (as on the #487 branch); no causal, spatiotemporal, material or independence criterion is built in, and failing it is not thereby being abstract. Concrete is not material: an idealist may count an actual experience as concrete. The world w is an element of the frame, a complete history rather than a time. Inhabitation of the world type or membership in the candidate domain is not population.
note: Stipulated for #536 so that the Cogito result has the exact shape of #487's PopulatedConcreteAt (branch codex/487-necessary-concrete-root, not merged). When #487 lands, one of the two should be defined from the other. A source-grounded criterion of concreteness is open (#544).
